assumptions: Pants and shirt vertices are lifted along normals (0.7 mm and 1.5 mm) because glTF cannot carry polygon offset, and the baked result visually matches the runtime-fixed result in the hero zoom.
The original is recovered from git (sha256 pinned in the script) instead of committing a second 14 MB copy.

jpeg-js 0.4.4 was added as an exactly pinned devDependency (pure JavaScript, BSD-3-Clause) because the repo had no JPEG codec and native sharp is not a declared dependency and could change the bytes per platform.
One minor speck remains at the left sleeve edge in the zoomed hero view, also present in the runtime-fixed version.
decisionsProposed: Clothing fixes for the Avaturn avatar live in the asset via scripts/bake-avatar-look.mjs, not at runtime; any change to the avatar clothing means editing the bake and re-running it from the pinned original.
Layering of nearly coincident clothing meshes is done by geometric normal lift in the bake, because glTF has no polygon offset.
lessonsProposed: When baking a render-state fix (polygonOffset) into glTF geometry, check it first on a zoomed screenshot: dropping it brought the collar and sleeve specks back until a vertex lift replaced it.
Gate bake scripts with a pinned input sha256 plus an in-file marker so they cannot compound, and keep the original in git history instead of duplicating a large binary.
In CDP readiness checks use gl.info.render.calls, since info.render.frames is undefined in this three version.
